gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Noto Sans Tai Tham reads like chalkboard lowercase pushed up toward the capitals. Paragraphs flow with a clearly visible inside to each c, while Irish Grover above brings sturdy, softly varied strokes.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Sturdy, fun letters up top, then tall and friendly ones below. Noto Sans Tai Viet pulls its terminals back from the curves, so text moves smoothly under Irish Grover.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-yi: Sturdy and fun, Irish Grover varies its strokes mildly, like a letterpress slug. Noto Sans Yi has a deep midsection and rounds left unsealed, so a page of it reads smooth and modern.
gen-irish-grover-gf-numans: Numans spreads its swollen lowercase wide, with s ends hanging far from the spine. What stands out is how tall, sturdy Irish Grover meets that loose tracking, every stroke solid and readable.
gen-irish-grover-gf-pathway-extreme: Fun and sturdy, Irish Grover makes its words look big and solid. Pathway Extreme sits below with stubby ascenders and clear openings in its rounds, leaving the heading room to stand out.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-ubuntu-sans: Commanding tube-like lettering up top, with a splayed c terminal. Tilt Neon takes the heading while Ubuntu Sans adds tubular strokes and big lowercase, so both feel bent from the same pipe.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-sofia-sans: Warnes spreads wide, its ink strokes tapering out before they touch. Sofia Sans stands tall in uniform strokes with open rounds, so paragraphs move along with a modern, steady feel.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans: Loud, cheerful lettering from Luckiest Guy, with its mean line set high. Shrink the heading and the shout fades; Noto Sans, with lowercase filling most of the letter height, does the talking.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Noto Sans Coptic lets its middle zone dominate each line. Give Luckiest Guy generous size so its plain, unshaded line carries the loudness, and let the sans-serif text stay modest beside it.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-oriya: A cheerful shout, from Luckiest Guy, then a friendly murmur. Noto Sans Oriya keeps small letters nearly capital height with generous curve gaps, while the heading's o stays equally thick all around.
